description: Hard and soft landscaping to front garden; alterations to front boundary wall and gates; installation of new gate to side
decision_conditions:
<p class="MsoListParagraph" style="">The materiality and mix of
the boundary treatments to the scale/extent proposed to the full width of the
site, together with the significant coverage of hardstanding to the site frontage
would result in development which would erode the historic openness of the site
and generate imbalance between hard and soft landscaping, creating an overly
urbanised and cluttered appearance that would be visually prominent within the
streetscape. The development is unsympathetic to, and out of keeping with, and
neither preserve or enhance the character and appearance of the Roxborough and
the Grove Conservation Area, a designated heritage asset, nor the special
character of the locally listed application dwelling, a non-designated heritage
asset. The identified harm would amount to ‘less than substantial’ harm to the
significance of the heritage assets, which would not be outweighed by public
benefits, contrary to Paragraph 215 of the National Planning Policy Framework
(NPPF, 2024). The proposals would fail to accord with the policy objectives of Paragraphs
212 and 216 of the NPPF (2024), Policy HC1 of the London Plan (2021) and Policy
HE1 of the Harrow Local Plan (2021-2041).&nbsp;<o:p></o:p></p>
